cues.en: One single scientist created three inventions that accidentally caused the deaths of millions of people,
cues.zh: 一位科学家独自做出了三项发明，这些发明意外导致数百万人死亡，

cues.en: including himself.
cues.zh: 包括他自己。

cues.en: Not only that, they decreased the average intelligence of people all around the world, increased crime rates, and caused two completely separate environmental disasters that we are still dealing with today.
cues.zh: 不仅如此，这些发明还降低了全世界人的平均智力，提高了犯罪率，并造成了两个完全独立的环境灾难，而我们至今仍在应对。

cues.en: Part of this video is sponsored by Wren. More about them at the end of the show.
cues.zh: 本期视频部分由 Wren 赞助。关于他们的更多内容，将在节目最后介绍。

cues.en: as a young chemist who had just finished his master's,
cues.zh: 作为一名刚拿到硕士学位的年轻化学家，

cues.en: Claire Patterson went to work on the Manhattan Project,
cues.zh: 克莱尔·帕特森加入了曼哈顿计划，

cues.en: building the first nuclear weapons.
cues.zh: 参与制造第一批核武器。

cues.en: His job was to concentrate uranium two thirty five, the fissile fuel for bombs, from the much more common uranium two thirty eight. And this required huge machines,
cues.zh: 他的工作是从更常见的铀-238中浓缩出铀-235——炸弹用的易裂变燃料。这需要巨大的机器，

cues.en: mass spectrometers,
cues.zh: 质谱仪，

cues.en: which separated the two types of uranium by their slight difference in mass.
cues.zh: 它们根据两种铀之间微小的质量差异将二者分离。

cues.en: After the war, Patterson went back to grad school to get his PhD.
cues.zh: 战后，帕特森回到研究生院攻读博士学位。

cues.en: He picked a research project that would take advantage of his experience with mass spectrometers,
cues.zh: 他选了一个能发挥自己质谱仪经验的研究项目，

cues.en: measuring the age of the earth.
cues.zh: 测量地球的年龄。

cues.en: Radioactive rocks are effectively
cues.zh: 放射性岩石实际上就是

cues.en: clocks.
cues.zh: 时钟。

cues.en: Uranium two thirty eight, for example, decays into thorium and then protactinium and then 12 more decays until it ends up as lead two zero six, which is stable.
cues.zh: 例如，铀-238会衰变成钍，再衰变成镤，之后又经过12次衰变，最终变成稳定的铅-206。

cues.en: The rate of this decay is consistent and can be measured. It takes four and a half billion years for half of a sample of u two thirty eight to decay into lead two zero six.
cues.zh: 这种衰变速率恒定，而且可以测量。铀-238样本的一半衰变成铅-206需要45亿年。

cues.en: Patterson's PhD project was to determine the age of the earth by measuring the ratio of uranium to lead in primordial
cues.zh: 帕特森的博士项目，是通过测量原始

cues.en: rocks.
cues.zh: 岩石中铀与铅的比例，来确定地球的年龄。

cues.en: But to calibrate his instrument, first, he used zircon crystals whose ages were known.
cues.zh: 但为了校准仪器，他首先使用了年龄已知的锆石晶体。

cues.en: Zircon is ideal for this purpose because when it forms, it contains trace amounts of uranium but absolutely no lead.
cues.zh: 锆石非常适合这个用途，因为它形成时含有微量铀，但完全没有铅。

cues.en: So any lead that you later find inside a zircon, you know must be the product of a uranium decay.
cues.zh: 所以后来在锆石里发现的任何铅，都必然是铀衰变的产物。

cues.en: Now, Patterson was tasked with measuring the lead content and another student, George Tilton, measured uranium.
cues.zh: 当时，帕特森负责测量铅含量，另一名学生乔治·蒂尔顿测量铀。

cues.en: Tilton's uranium measurements were fine. They matched predictions.
cues.zh: 蒂尔顿的铀测量结果没问题，和预测相符。

cues.en: But Patterson's lead measurements were all over the place, and they were many, many times higher than they expected. We take George's uranium and my lead.
cues.zh: 但帕特森的铅测量结果乱七八糟，而且比他们预期的高出许多许多倍。我们拿乔治测的铀和我的铅一对比。

cues.en: Not right, Patterson.
cues.zh: 不对，帕特森。

cues.en: There was lead there that didn't belong there.
cues.zh: 那里有本不该存在的铅。

cues.en: So where was all this extra lead coming from?
cues.zh: 那么，这些多出来的铅是从哪儿来的？

cues.en: That mystery would take over the rest of Claire Patterson's life and bring him to the literal ends of the earth.
cues.zh: 这个谜团将占据克莱尔·帕特森的余生，并把他带到真正的地球尽头。

cues.en: In nineteen o eight, a woman was driving across the Belle Isle Bridge in Detroit when her car stalled.
cues.zh: 1908年，一名女子开车经过底特律的贝尔岛大桥时，汽车熄火了。

cues.en: A passing motorist stopped to help. In those days, cars needed to be hand cranked to start.
cues.zh: 一名路过的司机停下来帮忙。那时候，汽车需要用手摇曲柄才能启动。

cues.en: He knelt down and turned the crank and the engine roared to life a little too suddenly.
cues.zh: 他蹲下身转动曲柄，引擎骤然咆哮着发动了。

cues.en: The man couldn't get out of the way. The crank handle hit him in the face and broke his jaw. He
cues.zh: 他躲闪不及，手摇曲柄直接砸在脸上，打碎了他的下颌骨。他

cues.en: died as a result of his injuries.
cues.zh: 最终因伤重不治身亡。

cues.en: His name was Byron Carter,
cues.zh: 他的名字叫 Byron Carter，

cues.en: and he was the founder of his own car company.
cues.zh: 他创办了自己的汽车公司。

cues.en: So he was well connected in the Detroit auto scene.
cues.zh: 因此他在底特律汽车界人脉很广。

cues.en: He counted among his close friends the founder of Cadillac, Henry Leland.
cues.zh: 他的密友中就包括 Cadillac 的创始人 Henry Leland。

cues.en: Leland was so distraught over his friend's death that he resolved to eliminate hand cranks from his vehicles.
cues.zh: 朋友的惨死让 Leland 悲痛欲绝，他下定决心要在自己的车上彻底淘汰手摇曲柄。

cues.en: Leland hired Charles Kettering to create a self starting car. And by 1911,
cues.zh: Leland 聘请了 Charles Kettering 来研发能自动启动的汽车。到了 1911 年，

cues.en: he had a working prototype.
cues.zh: 他就造出了可运行的原型车。

cues.en: Hand cranking was difficult and dangerous
cues.zh: 手摇启动既吃力又危险，

cues.en: and best left to men.
cues.zh: 基本上只能由成年男子来干。

cues.en: But a car that started itself
cues.zh: 但一辆能自动启动的汽车，

cues.en: changed
cues.zh: 改变了

cues.en: everything.
cues.zh: 一切。

cues.en: The world's first crankless car was the Cadillac model 30. It was much more powerful than cars before it. It had a top speed of 45 miles per hour and 40 horsepower,
cues.zh: 世界上第一辆免手摇汽车是 Cadillac Model 30。它的动力远超以往的车型，最高时速可达 45 英里，拥有 40 马力，

cues.en: double the Ford model t.
cues.zh: 是 Ford Model T 的两倍。

cues.en: The model 30 was a huge success for Cadillac, doubling the company's annual sales.
cues.zh: Model 30 让 Cadillac 大获成功，公司年销量直接翻了一番。

cues.en: But it had a problem.
cues.zh: 但它也带来了一个问题。

cues.en: It was deafeningly loud.
cues.zh: 它的噪音震耳欲聋。

cues.en: In internal combustion engines, a piston compresses the fuel air mixture, which is then ignited by a spark from the spark plug. The expanding hot gases push the piston back down.
cues.zh: 在内燃机中，活塞压缩油气混合物，随后被火花塞的电火花点燃，膨胀的高温气体会将活塞推回下方。

cues.en: The problem with the model 30 engine was it compressed the fuel air mixture more than previous models.
cues.zh: Model 30 引擎的问题在于，它对油气混合物的压缩比以往的车型更高。

cues.en: So much in fact that often the fuel would spontaneously combust
cues.zh: 压缩程度甚至高到燃料往往会直接自燃，

cues.en: before the spark from the spark plug. So rather than orderly perfectly timed explosions, you'd get multiple haphazard combustions leading to turbulent pressure waves inside the cylinder.
cues.zh: 赶在火花塞点火之前。这样一来，气缸内不再是井然有序、时机精准的爆炸，而是多次杂乱无章的燃烧，从而在气缸内部引发紊乱的压力波。

cues.en: The resulting sound led the problem to become known as engine knocking.
cues.zh: 由此产生的异响让这个问题被称为“引擎爆震”（engine knocking）。

cues.en: Knocking wasn't just hard on the ears, it hurt the engine's performance.
cues.zh: 爆震不仅刺耳，还会损害引擎的性能。

cues.en: It reduced power output and lowered fuel efficiency.
cues.zh: 它降低了动力输出，也削弱了燃油效率。

cues.en: The vibrations also damaged the piston and walls of the cylinder, shortening the life of the engine.
cues.zh: 剧烈的震动还会损坏活塞和气缸壁，缩短引擎的使用寿命。

cues.en: The good news was that engine knocking could be corrected by changing the fuel.
cues.zh: 好消息是，更换燃料就可以解决引擎爆震的问题。

cues.en: Different fuels can withstand different levels of compression before detonating.
cues.zh: 不同的燃料在爆燃前能承受的压缩程度各不相同。

cues.en: N heptane, for example, will spontaneously combust under only a little compression.
cues.zh: 例如，正庚烷（n-heptane）只需稍微压缩就会自燃。

cues.en: Iso octane on the other hand can withstand a much higher compression ratio before it auto ignites,
cues.zh: 而异辛烷（iso-octane）在自燃前可以承受高得多的压缩比，

cues.en: so it's much less likely to cause knocking.
cues.zh: 因此极不容易引起爆震。

cues.en: To quantify how much compression a fuel can withstand, scientists came up with the octane rating system. They arbitrarily set iso octane to have a rating of a 100 and n heptane a rating of zero.
cues.zh: 为了量化燃料能承受的压缩极限，科学家提出了辛烷值（octane rating）体系。他们人为规定异辛烷的辛烷值为 100，正庚烷为 0。

cues.en: Now real fuels aren't made up of only these two ingredients. They're a mix of lots of different hydrocarbons, but the octane rating tells you what mixture of octane and heptane gives equivalent performance.
cues.zh: 现实中的燃油并不只由这两种成分构成，而是多种碳氢化合物的混合物，但辛烷值能直观地告诉你，该燃油的抗爆性能相当于何种比例的辛烷与庚烷混合物。

cues.en: For example, 98 octane fuel can withstand the same compression as a mixture of 98% octane and 2% heptane. Now I'm gonna take a little bit of 98 octane fuel and put it in this
cues.zh: 例如，98辛烷值燃料能承受的压缩程度，与98%辛烷和2%庚烷的混合物相同。现在我要取一点98辛烷值燃料，放进这个

cues.en: piston,
cues.zh: 活塞里，

cues.en: and when I compress it,
cues.zh: 当我压缩它时，

cues.en: nothing happens, which is exactly what you'd expect.
cues.zh: 什么也不会发生，完全如你所料。

cues.en: This fuel can withstand a lot of compression. Diesel has an octane rating of 20, so it acts like a mixture of 20% isooctane and 80% n heptane. If I put a little bit of diesel in there,
cues.zh: 这种燃料能承受很大的压缩。柴油的辛烷值是20，所以它相当于20%异辛烷和80%正庚烷的混合物。如果我在里面加一点柴油，

cues.en: let's see what happens with the same compression ratio.
cues.zh: 看看在相同压缩比下会发生什么。

cues.en: There you go. You get a little explosion in there. That's because this is a low octane fuel. I mean, that's what diesel is meant to do. You compress it and it ignites, but you don't want this sort of fuel in an engine with spark plugs.
cues.zh: 这就对了。里面发生了一次小爆炸。因为这是低辛烷值燃料。我是说，柴油本来就是干这个的。你压缩它，它就点燃，但你不希望带火花塞的发动机用这种燃料。

cues.en: The reason fancy cars demand high octane fuel is to prevent knocking in their high compression, high performance engines.
cues.zh: 豪车要求高辛烷值燃料，是为了防止它们高压缩比、高性能发动机发生爆震。

cues.en: Kettering wanted to find an additive which would increase the octane rating of ordinary fuel and eliminate knocking in high compression engines.
cues.zh: Kettering 想找到一种添加剂，能提高普通燃料的辛烷值，并消除高压缩比发动机的爆震。

cues.en: So he hired 27 year old engineer Thomas Midgley junior.
cues.zh: 于是他雇用了27岁的工程师 Thomas Midgley junior。

cues.en: Midgley experimented with all sorts of compounds from melted butter and camphor to ethyl acetate and aluminum chloride.
cues.zh: Midgley 试验了各种化合物，从融化的黄油和樟脑，到乙酸乙酯和氯化铝。

cues.en: He later wrote, most of them had no more effect than spitting in the Great Lakes.
cues.zh: 他后来写道，其中大多数效果还不如往五大湖里吐口水。

cues.en: Ethanol was an interesting exception. It did stop the knocking, but you needed a lot of it, about 10% of the fuel mixture for it to be effective.
cues.zh: 乙醇是个有趣的例外。它确实能止住爆震，但你需要大量乙醇，约占燃料混合物的10%才有效。

cues.en: That much ethanol would be expensive and hard to turn a profit on. And Midgley was really after an additive that was cheap, easy to produce, and effective even at low concentrations.
cues.zh: 那么多乙醇会很贵，也很难赚钱。而 Midgley 真正想要的是一种便宜、易生产，即使低浓度也有效的添加剂。

cues.en: So he kept trying.
cues.zh: 所以他继续尝试。

cues.en: Then he hit on tellurium.
cues.zh: 然后他试到了碲。

cues.en: It worked wonderfully as an anti knock agent,
cues.zh: 它作为抗爆剂效果极好，

cues.en: but it had a terrible smell.
cues.zh: 但气味极其难闻。

cues.en: You couldn't get rid of it by changing clothes or bathing.
cues.zh: 换衣服或洗澡都去不掉。

cues.en: His wife was so offended by the stench that he had to sleep in the basement for seven months.
cues.zh: 他妻子被这臭味熏得受不了，他只好在地下室睡了七个月。

cues.en: Midgley wrote, I don't think that although this doubled the fuel economy, humanity would suffer this smell.
cues.zh: Midgley 写道，我不认为，即使这能让燃油经济性翻倍，人类会忍受这种气味。

cues.en: after five years of working on the problem, Midgley found what he thought was the perfect solution,
cues.zh: 在钻研这个问题五年后，Midgley 找到了他心目中的完美解决方案，

cues.en: tetraethyl lead. That's a lead atom right there in the center.
cues.zh: 四乙基铅。正中间那个就是铅原子。

cues.en: This additive was exactly what he was looking for. It stopped the knocking, it didn't smell, it was cheap to produce and readily available. Best of all, you only needed one part in a thousand for it to be effective.
cues.zh: 这种添加剂正是他要找的。它能止住爆震，没有气味，生产成本低且容易获得。最棒的是，只需千分之一就有效。

cues.en: In a call to Kettering, Midgley said, can you imagine how much money we're gonna make with this? We're gonna make $200,000,000,
cues.zh: 在给 Kettering 的电话中，Midgley 说，你能想象我们能靠这个赚多少钱吗？我们要赚 2 亿美元，

cues.en: maybe even more.
cues.zh: 甚至更多。

cues.en: That is over 3,000,000,000
cues.zh: 那是超过 30 亿

cues.en: in today's dollars.
cues.zh: 按今天的美元价值。

cues.en: Now for his discovery, the American Chemical Society gave him the prestigious Nichols Award and they asked him to do a series of public talks, but Midgley declined.
cues.zh: 因为这项发现，美国化学学会授予他享有盛誉的 Nichols Award，并请他做一系列公开演讲，但 Midgley 拒绝了。

cues.en: He and Kettering patented the process for making tetraethyl lead, and they called their new additive ethyl,
cues.zh: 他和 Kettering 为制造四乙基铅的工艺申请了专利，并把这种新添加剂叫作 ethyl，

cues.en: perhaps so it might be confused with another common additive, ethyl alcohol. They made no mention of lead.
cues.zh: 也许是想让它和另一种常见添加剂乙醇混淆。他们对铅只字未提。

cues.en: Then they teamed up with three of America's largest corporations, General Motors, DuPont, and Standard Oil of New Jersey to form the Ethyl Corporation.
cues.zh: 随后，他们与美国三家最大的公司——General Motors、DuPont 和 Standard Oil of New Jersey——联手成立了 Ethyl Corporation。

cues.en: Their marketing was brilliant.
cues.zh: 他们的营销非常高明。

cues.en: No man can look at the amazing record of accomplishment here in this research division without confidence that these men are going ahead with an eye to the future.
cues.zh: 任何人看到这个研究部门令人惊叹的成就记录，都不会怀疑这些人正着眼未来向前推进。

cues.en: Looking for new facts and principles which will make things better and make life easier for all of us.
cues.zh: 寻找新的事实和原理，让东西更好，让我们所有人的生活更轻松。

cues.en: At the nineteen twenty three Indianapolis five hundred, the top three finishers
cues.zh: 在 1923 年 Indianapolis 500 大赛上，前三名完赛者

cues.en: all used Ethyl,
cues.zh: 全都使用了 Ethyl，

cues.en: and the demand for leaded gasoline took off.
cues.zh: 含铅汽油的需求随之猛增。

cues.en: To keep up, Ethyl Corporation had to build a new chemical plant in New Jersey, but the project began terribly.
cues.zh: 为了跟上需求，Ethyl Corporation 不得不在新泽西建一座新化工厂，但项目一开始就糟透了。

cues.en: Within two months of operating, dozens of workers fell ill with lead poisoning.
cues.zh: 投产不到两个月，就有数十名工人因铅中毒病倒。

cues.en: Five of them died.
cues.zh: 其中五人死亡。

cues.en: To address the public outcry, Midgley held a press conference.
cues.zh: 为回应公众的强烈抗议，Midgley 召开了新闻发布会。

cues.en: And there, he poured tetraethyl lead onto his hands and he inhaled it for a full minute.
cues.zh: 在会上，他把四乙基铅倒在自己手上，还整整吸了一分钟。

cues.en: He claimed he could do this daily without harm.
cues.zh: 他声称自己每天这样做也不会有害。

cues.en: But Midgley
cues.zh: 但 Midgley

cues.en: knew the dangers.
cues.zh: 知道其中的危险。

cues.en: The reason he had turned down the public talks was because he spent much of 1923
cues.zh: 他拒绝公开演讲的原因，是他 1923 年的大部分时间

cues.en: in Florida,
cues.zh: 都在佛罗里达，

cues.en: where he himself was recovering from lead poisoning.
cues.zh: 在那里，他自己正从铅中毒中康复。

cues.en: He didn't go anywhere near his company's product if he could help it.
cues.zh: 只要能避免，他就绝不靠近自己公司的产品。

cues.en: Lead is dangerous even in small doses.
cues.zh: 铅即使剂量很小也很危险。

cues.en: It mimics calcium in our bodies, so there's no efficient way to get rid of it. And like calcium, lead can be stored in bones for years,
cues.zh: 它会在人体内冒充钙，所以没有高效的方法把它排出。而且和钙一样，铅能在骨骼中储存多年，

cues.en: meaning it can continue to poison the body long after the initial exposure.
cues.zh: 这意味着在初次接触很久之后，它仍能继续毒害身体。

cues.en: The organ most sensitive to lead is the brain.
cues.zh: 对铅最敏感的器官是大脑。

cues.en: Lead breaks down the myelin sheath around axons and prevents the release of neurotransmitters.
cues.zh: 铅会破坏轴突周围的髓鞘，并阻止神经递质释放。

cues.en: That's why common symptoms of lead poisoning are headaches,
cues.zh: 所以铅中毒的常见症状是头痛、

cues.en: memory loss, and tingling in the hands and feet,
cues.zh: 记忆力减退，以及手脚发麻，

cues.en: and children are particularly susceptible.
cues.zh: 而儿童尤其易受影响。

cues.en: Lead exposure can cause permanent learning disorders and behavioral problems,
cues.zh: 接触铅可导致永久性的学习障碍和行为问题，

cues.en: and the dangers of lead had been known for hundreds of years. Already in 1786,
cues.zh: 而铅的危险已经为人所知数百年。早在 1786 年，

cues.en: Benjamin Franklin remarked that lead had been used for far too long considering its known toxicity.
cues.zh: Benjamin Franklin 就说过，考虑到铅已知的毒性，它被使用的时间实在太久了。

cues.en: You will observe with concern how long a useful truth may be known and exist before it is generally received and practiced on.
cues.zh: 你会忧心地看到，一个有价值的真理在被普遍接受和实践之前，可能早已为人所知并存在多久。

cues.en: He would have been aghast to learn that nearly a hundred and fifty years later, scientists plan to add lead to fuel.
cues.zh: 如果得知近一百五十年后，科学家计划往燃料里加铅，他一定会大为震惊。

cues.en: Doctors and public health officials from MIT, Harvard, Yale, and the US Health Service wrote to Midgley and warned them against producing tetraethyl lead. They called lead a creeping and malicious poison and a serious menace to public health.
cues.zh: 来自 MIT、Harvard、Yale 和美国公共卫生署的医生与公共卫生官员写信给 Midgley，警告他们不要生产四乙基铅。他们把铅称为一种悄然蔓延的恶意毒物，是对公共卫生的严重威胁。

cues.en: Their concerns
cues.zh: 他们的担忧

cues.en: were dismissed.
cues.zh: 被驳回了。

cues.en: This model shows how just the right amount of fluid containing tetraethyl lead and dye is added to the gasoline.
cues.zh: 这个模型展示了如何把适量含四乙基铅和染料的液体加入汽油。

cues.en: No one doubted that a lot of lead was bad for you, but how much harm could a little lead do?
cues.zh: 没人怀疑大量铅有害，但少量铅能造成多大危害？

cues.en: By the nineteen fifties, millions of motorists globally were burning lead in their cars and releasing it into the air.
cues.zh: 到 20 世纪 50 年代，全球数百万驾车者在汽车中燃烧铅，并将其释放到空气中。

cues.en: Some of that lead ended up on Claire Patterson's zircon samples preventing him from determining their age.
cues.zh: 其中一些铅落在了 Claire Patterson 的锆石样品上，使他无法测定它们的年龄。

cues.en: he moved to Caltech where he built a new lab from scratch.
cues.zh: 他搬到 Caltech，从零建起一个新实验室。

cues.en: Suspicious of environmental contamination,
cues.zh: 他怀疑存在环境污染，

cues.en: he tore the electrical cables out of the walls to remove the lead solder.
cues.zh: 于是把墙里的电缆拽出来，以去除含铅焊料。

cues.en: He cleaned the floors and benches daily with ammonia and made sure that air was always being blown out of the lab.
cues.zh: 他每天用氨水清洁地板和实验台，并确保空气始终从实验室向外吹。

cues.en: To go inside, you had to wear a plastic bunny suit. Patterson basically invented the clean room.
cues.zh: 进实验室必须穿塑料防尘服。Patterson 基本上发明了洁净室。

cues.en: Inside that room, he turned his attention to the oldest rocks in the solar system,
cues.zh: 在那间实验室里，他把注意力转向太阳系中最古老的岩石，

cues.en: meteorites.
cues.zh: 陨石。

cues.en: All the original rocks on earth had long since been destroyed by tectonic activity.
cues.zh: 地球上所有原始岩石早已被构造活动摧毁。

cues.en: But meteorites
cues.zh: 但陨石

cues.en: come from asteroids,
cues.zh: 来自小行星，

cues.en: which formed around the same time as Earth.
cues.zh: 它们与地球大约在同一时期形成。

cues.en: They have just been drifting through space until they entered the Earth's atmosphere.
cues.zh: 它们一直只是在太空中漂移，直到进入地球大气层。

cues.en: So the best way to measure the age of the Earth was to measure the age of meteorites.
cues.zh: 所以测量地球年龄的最佳方法，就是测量陨石的年龄。

cues.en: Patterson
cues.zh: Patterson

cues.en: measured five meteorites,
cues.zh: 测量了五块陨石，

cues.en: each with three different radiometric dating techniques,
cues.zh: 每块都用三种不同的放射性测年技术，

cues.en: and he found they were all
cues.zh: 他发现它们全都

cues.en: years old.
cues.zh: 年历史。

cues.en: That number is within point 15%
cues.zh: 这个数字与目前公认的地球年龄值相差不到 0.15%。

cues.en: of the currently accepted value for the age of the earth. You know, before Patterson's experiment, people thought the earth was a billion years younger.
cues.zh: 你知道，在 Patterson 的实验之前，人们认为地球比实际年轻十亿年。

cues.en: So Patterson had done it. He measured the age of the earth,
cues.zh: 所以 Patterson 成功了。他测出了地球的年龄，

cues.en: but he wasn't done getting rid of lead contaminants.
cues.zh: 但他清除铅污染物的任务还没完。

cues.en: Public concern about lead exposure had continued to grow, but president of Standard Oil, Frank Howard pushed back saying, we do not feel justified in giving up what has come to the industry like a gift from heaven on the possibility that a hazard may be involved in it.
cues.zh: 公众对铅暴露的担忧持续增长，但 Standard Oil 总裁 Frank Howard 反驳说：我们并不认为，仅仅因为可能存在危害，就有理由放弃这种对行业而言宛如天赐之物的东西。

cues.en: Scientists
cues.zh: 科学家们

cues.en: funded by the Ethel Corporation claimed that lead was a natural part of our environment and therefore not harmful to people.
cues.zh: 由 Ethel Corporation 资助的科学家声称，铅是我们环境中的天然组成部分，因此对人无害。

cues.en: But Patterson wondered
cues.zh: 但 Patterson 想知道

cues.en: just how natural is the lead in our environment
cues.zh: 我们环境中的铅到底有多天然

cues.en: And he had just the skills to find out.
cues.zh: 而他恰好具备查明这一点的技能。

cues.en: He began by measuring lead in the oceans. If it were natural, he expected the concentration of lead to be the same regardless of depth.
cues.zh: 他先从测量海洋中的铅含量开始。如果铅是自然存在的，他预计无论深浅，铅的浓度都应该是一样的。

cues.en: But if lead pollution had increased recently, it would be more concentrated near the surface.
cues.zh: 但如果是近期的铅污染加剧，表层海水的浓度就会更高。

cues.en: He took samples in the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans down to a depth of four kilometers.
cues.zh: 他在太平洋和大西洋采集了深达四公里的样本。

cues.en: And sure enough, lead concentrations were nearly 10 times higher near the surface.
cues.zh: 果不其然，表层的铅浓度高出了近十倍。

cues.en: Lead pollution was clearly recent,
cues.zh: 铅污染显然发生在近代，

cues.en: but when exactly had it occurred?
cues.zh: 但究竟是什么时候开始的？

cues.en: To find out, Patterson had to go to Greenland and Antarctica.
cues.zh: 为了查明真相，Patterson 必须前往格陵兰岛和南极洲。

cues.en: Ice cores record the level of lead in the air going back thousands of years.
cues.zh: 冰芯记录了数千年来空气中的铅含量。

cues.en: The levels of lead in the atmosphere have been elevated for the last forty five hundred years.
cues.zh: 过去 4500 年间，大气中的铅含量一直在升高。

cues.en: All of it is due to human activity, mainly smelting ores to make metal.
cues.zh: 这全都是人类活动造成的，主要是冶炼矿石提取金属。

cues.en: You can see the rise and fall of the Greek and Roman Empires,
cues.zh: 你能从中看到希腊和罗马帝国的兴衰，

cues.en: the dip caused by the Black Death in the thirteen hundreds,
cues.zh: 看到 14 世纪黑死病造成的骤降，

cues.en: and of course, the spike in the twentieth century due to industrialization
cues.zh: 当然，还有 20 世纪因工业化

cues.en: and tetraethyl lead.
cues.zh: 和四乙基铅导致的暴增。

cues.en: So what did this do to people?
cues.zh: 那么，这对人类造成了什么影响？

cues.en: Well, Patterson looked at the lead levels in the teeth and bones of recently deceased Americans.
cues.zh: Patterson 检测了近期去世的美国人牙齿和骨骼中的铅含量。

cues.en: And for comparison, he measured the lead in bones and teeth of Peruvian and Egyptian mummies.
cues.zh: 作为对比，他还测量了秘鲁和埃及木乃伊骨骼与牙齿中的铅。

cues.en: Since they lived over sixteen hundred years ago, they would have been exposed to much less lead in their lifetimes.
cues.zh: 由于他们生活在 1600 多年前，一生中接触到的铅要少得多。

cues.en: He expected to find modern Americans had about a 100 times as much lead in their bones,
cues.zh: 他原以为现代美国人骨骼中的铅含量大概会高出 100 倍左右，

cues.en: but results showed it was closer to a factor of a thousand.
cues.zh: 但结果显示，实际高出将近一千倍。

cues.en: Twentieth century Americans had a thousand times more lead in their bones than their ancestors.
cues.zh: 20 世纪美国人骨骼中的铅含量是他们祖先的一千倍。

cues.en: Studies of baby teeth revealed that even lead exposure well below the level considered safe resulted in delayed learning,
cues.zh: 对乳牙的研究显示，哪怕铅暴露量远低于公认的安全标准，也会导致学习迟缓、

cues.en: decreased IQ,
cues.zh: 智商下降，

cues.en: and increased behavioral problems.
cues.zh: 以及行为问题增多。

cues.en: And there is a a broad consensus
cues.zh: 而且大家已经形成了广泛的共识——

cues.en: on the part of everybody except the lead industry and its spokesman that lead is extremely toxic at extremely low doses.
cues.zh: 除了铅工业界及其代言人，所有人都认同即使极低剂量的铅也具有极高的毒性。

cues.en: A follow-up study showed that those with higher levels of lead in their baby teeth were many times more likely to fail out of high school.
cues.zh: 后续研究表明，乳牙中铅含量较高的人，高中辍学的几率要高出数倍。

cues.en: As a result of studies like these, the CDC's guidelines for the acceptable level of lead in children's blood dropped from sixty micrograms per deciliter down to three point five.
cues.zh: 正是由于这些研究，CDC 指南中儿童血铅的可接受标准从每分升 60 微克骤降到了 3.5 微克。

cues.en: And as far as we know today, there is no safe level of lead.
cues.zh: 而就我们今天所知，铅根本不存在所谓的“安全水平”。

cues.en: Globally, lead is believed to be responsible for nearly two thirds of all unexplained intellectual disability.
cues.zh: 在全球范围内，近三分之二不明原因的智力障碍都被认为与铅有关。

cues.en: According to a study published in 2022,
cues.zh: 根据 2022 年发表的一项研究，

cues.en: more than half of the current US population,
cues.zh: 目前超过半数的美国人，
也就是 1.7 亿

cues.en: people, were exposed to high levels of lead in early childhood.
cues.zh: 人，在童年早期都曾暴露于高浓度的铅环境中。

cues.en: Those born between 1951
and 1980
cues.zh: 到1980年间出生的人

cues.en: are disproportionately affected.
cues.zh: 受害程度格外严重。

cues.en: The authors estimate that in aggregate,
cues.zh: 研究人员估计，总体而言，

cues.en: lead caused a loss of more than 800,000,000
cues.zh: 铅导致了超过8亿点

cues.en: IQ points.
cues.zh: 智商的损失。

cues.en: The world is less intelligent today because of leaded gasoline.
cues.zh: 如今整个世界都因为含铅汽油变得更不聪明了。

cues.en: But there are even more troubling correlations.
cues.zh: 但还有更令人不安的相关性。

cues.en: The US saw a steady rise in crime from the nineteen seventies to the nineteen nineties.
cues.zh: 从20世纪70年代到90年代，美国的犯罪率持续攀升。

cues.en: Then it abruptly declined.
cues.zh: 随后却突然断崖式下降。

cues.en: This graph looks eerily similar to a plot of preschool blood lead levels just offset by twenty years.
cues.zh: 这张图表与学龄前儿童血铅水平的走势惊人地相似，只是滞后了20年。

cues.en: The obvious question is, did kids who were exposed to higher levels of lead grow up to commit more crimes than they otherwise would have?
cues.zh: 显而易见的问题是：暴露在高浓度铅环境下的儿童，长大后是否比其他人更容易犯罪？

cues.en: You might think this is just a spurious correlation,
cues.zh: 你可能会觉得这只是伪相关，

cues.en: but the same pattern appears in many countries, including Britain, Canada, and Australia.
cues.zh: 但同样的规律出现在了许多国家，包括英国、加拿大和澳大利亚。

cues.en: And we know there's a causal connection between lead exposure and antisocial or violent behavior.
cues.zh: 而且我们知道，铅暴露与反社会或暴力行为之间存在因果关联。

cues.en: A study of 340
cues.zh: 一项针对340名

cues.en: teenagers found that those who were arrested were four times as likely to have elevated lead in their bones than similar demographic controls who didn't have run ins with the law.
cues.zh: 青少年的研究发现，被捕者骨骼中铅含量超标的概率，是没有违法前科的同背景对照组的四倍。

cues.en: Now this doesn't mean that lead is responsible for all of the increase in crime, but it's very likely responsible for some of it.
cues.zh: 这并不意味着犯罪率上升全都是铅造成的，但它极可能是诱因之一。

cues.en: Now it's tough to estimate the precise death toll of lead.
cues.zh: 目前很难精确估计铅造成的致死人数。

cues.en: One of its lesser known effects is a hardening of the arteries
cues.zh: 它一个较少人知的影响是导致动脉硬化，

cues.en: leading to increased cardiovascular
cues.zh: 进而增加心血管

cues.en: disease.
cues.zh: 疾病的发生。

cues.en: A study from 2018 found lead was likely responsible for two hundred and fifty thousand heart disease deaths per year in The US.
cues.zh: 2018年的一项研究发现，在美国，每年可能有多达25万人死于铅引发的心脏病。

cues.en: Assuming a constant rate over the past century, that amounts to twenty five million deaths in The US alone.
cues.zh: 假设过去一个世纪里这一比例保持不变，仅在美国就相当于有2500万人死亡。

cues.en: Globally,
cues.zh: 而在全球范围内，

cues.en: the figure may approach a hundred million.
cues.zh: 这一数字可能接近一亿。

cues.en: Most of those deaths are due to Midgley's decision to put lead in gasoline,
cues.zh: 这些死亡大多归咎于 Midgley 决定在汽油中加铅，

cues.en: a substance he knew firsthand was toxic, but he did it anyway to maximize profits.
cues.zh: 他亲身体会过这种物质的毒性，但为了利益最大化，他还是这么做了。

cues.en: And the problem is not over. Current estimates of deaths caused by lead range from five hundred to nine hundred thousand per year. The 2020 UNICEF report warns that one in three children globally,
cues.zh: 而且问题还没结束。目前估计每年因铅致死的人数在50万到90万之间。UNICEF 2020年的报告警告称，全球三分之一的儿童，

cues.en: that's over eight hundred million children, have blood lead levels at or above five micrograms per deciliter.
cues.zh: 也就是超过8亿儿童，血铅水平达到或超过了每分升5微克。

cues.en: A lot of this lead now comes from batteries and industrial processes,
cues.zh: 如今许多铅来自于电池和工业生产，

cues.en: but some is still due to Mitchelie's invention.
cues.zh: 但有些仍要归咎于 Mitchelie 的这项发明。

cues.en: Now after Mitchelie's success with Ethel, he was put in charge of another engineering project. GM wasn't just making cars, but also household appliances
cues.zh: 在 Mitchelie 凭借 Ethel 大获成功后，他又负责了另一个工程项目。当时 GM 不仅制造汽车，也生产家用电器，

cues.en: and fridges had a problem. The two most common gases used as refrigerants were methyl formate and sulfur dioxide.
cues.zh: 而当时的冰箱有个棘手的问题。最常用的两种制冷气体是甲酸甲酯和二氧化硫。

cues.en: One is highly toxic, the other is flammable.
cues.zh: 一种剧毒，另一种易燃。

cues.en: Midgley was tasked with creating a safer alternative,
cues.zh: Midgley 受命研发一种更安全的替代品，

cues.en: and in 1928,
he developed a nontoxic and nonflammable refrigerant,
cues.zh: 他开发出了一种无毒且不易燃的制冷剂——

cues.en: dichlorodifluoromethane.
cues.zh: 二氯二氟甲烷。

cues.en: GM called this new product Freon and to demonstrate Freon safety during the unveiling at the American Chemical Society, Midgley inhaled a lung full of this gas and blew out a candle.
cues.zh: GM 将这种新产品命名为 Freon。为了在 American Chemical Society 的发布会上证明其安全性，Midgley 深吸了一大口这种气体，然后吹灭了一支蜡烛。

cues.en: In the following decades, CFCs like Freon became very popular and were used as solvents and aerosols.
cues.zh: 在接下来的几十年里，像 Freon 这样的 CFC（氟氯烃）广受欢迎，被大量用作溶剂和气雾推进剂。

cues.en: The problem is CFCs
cues.zh: 问题在于，CFC

cues.en: are light and stable. When released into the atmosphere,
cues.zh: 既轻便又稳定。一旦排放到大气中，

cues.en: they climb up into the stratosphere where they can remain for fifty to a hundred years. But if a CFC molecule is hit by an ultraviolet photon of just the right energy, it breaks apart releasing a chlorine atom. And this chlorine atom can then react with ozone
cues.zh: 它们就会上升到平流层，并在那里停留 50 到 100 年。但只要 CFC 分子被能量恰到好处的紫外线光子击中，就会分解并释放出一个氯原子。而这个氯原子随后会与臭氧发生反应，

cues.en: breaking it apart into chlorine monoxide and oxygen gas.
cues.zh: 将其分解为一氧化氯和氧气。

cues.en: The result was another environmental disaster, the hole in the ozone layer. With less ozone, more UV light penetrates the atmosphere increasing the rates of skin cancer and cataracts.
cues.zh: 结果导致了另一场环境灾难：臭氧层空洞。随着臭氧减少，更多紫外线穿透大气层，导致皮肤癌和白内障的发病率上升。

cues.en: Plus CFCs
cues.zh: 此外，CFC

cues.en: are potent greenhouse gases. Per kilogram, they produce 10,000 times more warming than c o two. The historian John McNeil wrote that Midgley had more impact on the atmosphere than any other single organism in Earth's history.
cues.zh: 还是极强的温室气体。按单位质量计算，它们产生的温室效应是二氧化碳的 10,000 倍。历史学家 John McNeil 写道，Midgley 对地球大气的影响，超过了地球历史上任何单一生物。

cues.en: An agreement to phase out CFCs,
cues.zh: 旨在逐步淘汰 CFC 的协议——

cues.en: the Montreal Protocol went into effect in 1989,
cues.zh: 《Montreal Protocol》于 1989 年正式生效，

cues.en: and the ozone layer is now showing signs of recovery, although it'll take many more decades to fully recover.
cues.zh: 如今臭氧层已出现恢复的迹象，尽管要完全康复还需要好几十年。

cues.en: at the age of 51, Midgley contracted polio and became physically disabled.
cues.zh: 51 岁的 Midgley 患上小儿麻痹症，导致身体瘫痪。

cues.en: So to help him get up, he devised a mechanical bed controlled by a series of ropes and pulleys.
cues.zh: 为了方便自己起床，他设计了一张由一系列绳索和滑轮控制的机械床。

cues.en: while using the contraption,
cues.zh: 在使用这套装置时，

cues.en: he became tangled in the ropes and died of strangulation.
cues.zh: 他被绳索缠住，窒息身亡。

cues.en: Thanks to the work of Claire Patterson, it became clear that the lead in our environment is not natural.
cues.zh: 多亏了 Claire Patterson 的工作，人们终于明白，环境中的铅绝非天然存在。

cues.en: Burning lead in combustion engines spread the toxic element across the planet into the air, oceans,
cues.zh: 内燃机燃烧含铅汽油，将这种有毒元素扩散到了全球的大气、海洋、

cues.en: the snow at the South Pole and even our bones.
cues.zh: 南极的积雪，甚至我们的骨骼之中。

cues.en: Japan was the first to ban leaded fuel in cars in 1986,
cues.zh: 日本在 1986 年率先禁止在汽车中使用含铅汽油，

cues.en: but other countries soon followed suit.
cues.zh: 其他国家也很快纷纷效仿。

cues.en: Algeria was the last to do so in 2021.
cues.zh: 阿尔及利亚在 2021 年成为最后一个禁用的国家。

cues.en: The UN calculates that the elimination of lead from gas saves over a million lives per year and $2,450,000,000,000.
cues.zh: 联合国测算，汽油无铅化每年挽救了 100 多万人的生命，并节省了 2.45 万亿美元。

cues.en: But leaded gas is still used, by the way, in piston driven airplane engines. That's now the largest source of lead emissions into the air in The US.
cues.zh: 顺便提一句，含铅汽油目前仍在活塞式飞机发动机中使用。这已成为全美空气中最大的铅排放源。

cues.en: You will observe with concern how long a useful truth may be known and exist before it is generally received and practiced on.
cues.zh: 你会忧心地发现，一条有益的真理往往在被发现很久之后，才能被大众普遍接受并付诸实践。

cues.en: When I first learned about Thomas Midgley and Claire Patterson,
cues.zh: 当我第一次了解 Thomas Midgley 和 Claire Patterson 的故事时，

cues.en: I was amazed by how much harm or how much good a single person could do to the environment, which brings me to the sponsor of this video, Wren, an organization that's taking action on climate change. I think it's important that we tackle the climate crisis both by lobbying for systemic change and by making more environmentally friendly choices ourselves.
cues.zh: 我惊叹于一个人竟能对环境造成如此巨大的破坏，或带来如此深远的益处。这也引出了本期视频的赞助商 Wren，一个致力于应对气候变化的组织。我认为，应对气候危机不仅需要推动系统性变革，也需要我们自身做出更环保的选择，这两者都至关重要。

cues.en: On Wren's website, you can calculate how much carbon you emit and which activities have the greatest impact.
cues.zh: 在 Wren 的网站上，你可以计算自己的碳排放量，以及哪些活动影响最大。

cues.en: And if you like, you can offset your emissions through a monthly subscription.
cues.zh: 如果愿意，你可以通过月度订阅来抵消排放。

cues.en: The funds raised go to support a variety of projects that reduce greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.
cues.zh: 筹集的资金用于支持各种减少大气中温室气体的项目。

cues.en: One project I particularly like involves collecting up flammable dead wood from California forests.
cues.zh: 我特别喜欢的一个项目，是从加州森林中收集易燃的枯木。

cues.en: This helps prevent wildfires.
cues.zh: 这有助于预防野火。

cues.en: Plus, the collected wood is converted into biochar,
cues.zh: 此外，收集的木材会被转化为生物炭，

cues.en: a material that locks up the carbon inside for thousands of years. Once you sign up to offset your carbon footprint, you'll receive monthly updates from the projects you support.
cues.zh: 这种材料能将碳封存其中数千年。一旦你注册抵消自己的碳足迹，就会每月收到你所支持项目的进展更新。

cues.en: It's completely transparent with photos and details of every tree planted,
cues.zh: 整个过程完全透明，包含每棵树的照片和详细信息，

cues.en: every acre reforested,
cues.zh: 每一英亩重新造林，

cues.en: every ton of carbon offset. And for the first 100 people who sign up using the link in the description, I will personally pay for the first month of your subscription.
cues.zh: 每一吨碳抵消。对于前 100 位通过简介中的链接注册的人，我会亲自支付你订阅的首月费用。

cues.en: So I wanna thank Wren for supporting Veritasium,
cues.zh: 所以我要感谢 Wren 对 Veritasium 的支持，

cues.en: and I wanna thank you for watching.
cues.zh: 也感谢你的观看。
